title: Changesets v3: Bumps Peer Dependents by Patch and Ships ESM Only with an 88% Smaller Install
gist: Changesets v3.0, released 11 August 2026 as its first major release in seven years, ships ESM-only with an install roughly 87% smaller (16.1MB to 2.1MB) and a rebuilt CLI, and changes peer-dependency updates from a major to a patch bump for dependents -- a widely requested semver fix that a rival maintainer (Bumpy) says merely swaps one hardcoded extreme for another.

insights.claim: Changesets v3.0 landed on 11 August 2026, its first major release in the seven years since v2, led by a refreshed maintainer team of Mateusz Burzynski, Bjorn Lu and Adam Haglund working through a public v3 release plan, and arrives alongside a new documentation site and a matching changesets/action v2, with the project already seeing more than 3 million weekly downloads.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: At 3M+ weekly downloads, changes to Changesets' behavior ripple across a large share of the JavaScript monorepo ecosystem's release pipelines.

insights.claim: Changesets is an MIT-licensed tool for versioning and changelogs focused on monorepos, where contributors declare how their changes should be released and the CLI turns those declarations into version bumps, changelog entries and registry publishes; v2 remains available on a maintenance branch after v3's release.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams are not forced into an immediate migration since v2 continues to receive maintenance, lowering upgrade urgency.
insights.locator: Changesets is an MIT licensed tool

insights.claim: The v3 cleanup made all packages ESM-only, requiring Node.js 22.11 or newer plus pnpm 10, npm 10.9 or Yarn 4.5.2 (with Yarn Classic dropped), and cut install size from 16.1MB to 2.1MB and dependencies from 95 to 39 by moving internally to tsdown, rolldown, vitest and oxfmt.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: An ~87% install-size reduction meaningfully cuts CI install time and dependency-surface risk at the scale of 3M+ weekly downloads, and reflects the broader JS tooling trend toward Rust/Rolldown-based leaner toolchains.
insights.quote: The cleanup cut install size from 16.1MB to 2.1MB and dependencies from 95 to 39
insights.locator: All packages are now ESM only

insights.claim: Changelog formatting no longer bundles its own copy of Prettier; instead the new @changesets/format module auto-detects whichever formatter -- Prettier, oxfmt, deno or dprint -- the host project already uses.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Removes a redundant bundled dependency and lets teams standardize on whichever formatter they've already adopted elsewhere in their toolchain.
insights.locator: Changelog formatting no longer pulls in its own Prettier copy

insights.claim: The headline behavior change in v3 is that a peer dependency update now gives dependents a patch bump rather than a major one, reversing years of complaints -- including issue 1011, where a design-system monorepo maintainer said the old major-bump behavior 'feels like it is sending the wrong message and not honouring semver.'
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Monorepo maintainers on Changesets should expect materially fewer forced major-version releases propagating across their dependency graphs after upgrading to v3.
insights.quote: feels like it is sending the wrong message and not honouring semver

insights.claim: Bumpy, a recently launched competing tool, argues v3 'hardcodes the opposite extreme' since it now treats every peer dependency change as non-breaking and, like v2, gives users no way to configure that propagation behavior, though Bumpy's maintainers still credit v3 with fixing many long-standing complaints while noting gaps such as missing pnpm catalog support and an unchanged prerelease design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Signals an unresolved design tension in monorepo versioning around configurable peer-dependency propagation that a challenger tool could exploit as a differentiator.

insights.claim: The CLI was rebuilt on cac for argument parsing and clack for prompts, fixing a bug where cancelled prompts crashed the process, and adds new pack and publish-plan commands aligned with the e18e community's recommended build-pack-publish sequence, while the v2 GitHub Action exposes sub-actions so teams using npm trusted publishing can narrow their publish permissions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The trusted-publishing sub-action support is directly relevant to supply-chain security posture for teams publishing packages to npm.
insights.locator: The CLI was rebuilt on cac

insights.claim: Upgrading to v3 requires renamed commands and flags (e.g. 'changeset tag' becomes 'changeset git-tag', '--sinceMaster' becomes '--since=main') plus configuration changes, including replacing the prettier config key with format and no longer versioning private packages by default unless opted back in via privatePackages, making the migration real configuration work rather than a drop-in upgrade.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams should budget explicit migration time rather than assuming the major version bump is purely internal plumbing.

insights.claim: changeset version now exits with code 1 when there is nothing to release, which one team's release playbook warns means 'any script that runs it unconditionally under set -e will now fail on an empty release,' a subtle CI breakage risk for teams that don't adjust their release scripts before upgrading.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams should audit CI pipelines that invoke changeset version unconditionally under set -e before upgrading, to avoid silent pipeline failures on empty release cycles.
insights.quote: any script that runs it unconditionally under set -e will now fail on an empty release.
insights.locator: changeset version now exits with code 1

insights.claim: Against semantic-release, which infers versions from conventional commits, and release-it, Changesets keeps its distinctive model of contributors writing release intent into reviewable markdown files as pull requests; v3 does not change that model, it only makes it cheaper to install and better behaved around peer dependencies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: For teams choosing a versioning tool, the core trade-off between explicit human-authored release notes and automated commit-based inference is unchanged -- v3 only fixes execution friction, not the underlying philosophy.
